lawyer: Menhazuddin Ahmed, Advocate ----- For the Petitioner.
parties:
Bazlur Rahman Sikder ------ Petitioner
vs.
Tahera Begum Shamima ------ Plaintiff Opposite Party
full_judgment:
Md. Abdul Karim J: This application at the instance of the husband-petitioner under section 115 of the Code of Civil Procedure is directed against the judgment and decree dated 3-3-98 passed by the learned Subordinate Judge. 2nd Court, Bogra, in Family Appeal No. 14/1997 affirming the Judgment and decree dated 28-4-1997 passed by the Family Court (Second Assistant Judge, Bogra in Family Suit No. 48 of 1997 awarding dower and maintenance to the wife for the period of iddat for a sum of Taka 24,501.00 and in addition allowing maintenance for two minor sons at the rate of Taka 2000.00 a month till attainment of majority by them. 

 2. Facts of the case, in short, are that defendant-petitioner Bazlur Rahman Sikder married plaintiff-opposite party Mrs Tahera Begum Shamima on 11-5-77 and that they have two sons out of the wedlock. This marriage was terminated by the husband through divorce on 3-4-94. After this divorce the wife filed Family Suit No.48 of 1997 before the Family Court and Senior Assistant Judge, Second Court, Bogra, for dower and maintenance for the period of iddat. The defendant did not deny the marriage with the plaintiff on 11-5-77 and having two sons out of this marriage. The trial Court decreed the suit for a sum of Taka 24,501.00 on account of dower and maintenance for the period of iddat (maintenance for wife for three months at the rate of Taka 1500.00 a month). The husband did not prefer any appeal against this judgment and decree passed by the Family Court in Family Suit No.48 of 1997. An appeal was, however, preferred by the wife being Family Appeal No.14 of 1997 claiming maintenance for two minor sons and the appellate Court allowed the appeal on contest affirming the Judgment and decree passed by the Court below in respect of Taka 24,501.00 on account of dower and maintenance to the wife for the period of iddat. The appellate Court further, allowed Taka 2,000.00 a month on account of maintenance of the two minor sons till attainment of majority by them. The present revisional application is directed against this order of the appellate Court directing maintenance for two minor sons, who have been living with their mother at Bogra in the house of the maternal Grandfather. 

 4. In her evidence PW 1 Tahera Begum mentions that she married the petitioner, who was posted as Sub-Divisional Officer at Bogra, and when she was living as wife of the petitioner, she came to know that he had his first wife alive with four children, which had been kept concealed from her at the time of the marriage. She lived with the petitioner as his wife for 17 years and they have two sons from this marriage. After her marriage with the petitioner, he married one Rabeya as his third wife and one Fatema as his fourth wife. The relationship between PW 1 and the petitioner took a turn for the worse after she came to know about subsequent marriages by her husband. On first April, 1993, PW 1 came to the house of her sister and from there she came to the house of her father and she came to know of her husband's fifth marriage. Thereafter she came to Dhaka when her husband drove her away. This followed divorce by the husband. Thereafter she was compelled to file a suit claiming dower and maintenance and the suit was decreed as mentioned at the outset.
